prompt: A polynomial graph has two ends, called its ARMS. For $p(x) = -2x^4 + 3x$, how many of the two arms point UP?
hint: Only the leading term $-2x^4$ decides where the arms point.

hints.text: Only the leading term $-2x^4$ decides where the arms point.
The degree $4$ is EVEN, so both arms point the same way. The leading coefficient $-2$ is negative.
Even degree plus a negative leader means both arms point DOWN, so $0$ arms point up.

explanation: Even degree: both arms go the same direction.
Negative leading coefficient: that direction is DOWN.
So neither arm points up — the answer is $0$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test giant numbers
steps: Both far ends dive down, so no arm points up.
